rules.text: Objects with distinctive moving features, or with glass, draw in two or more calls. All others in one.

Max 3000 tris per occupied grid cell. Measured as tris ÷ (max(0.49, w × d) × max(0.7, h)) over the bounding box: a 2 × 2 floor tile is judged on four cells, and an asset smaller than 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 is judged as if it were that size.
Nothing is taller than 6 units, except env-terrain-mountain.
special is a material tag and a joker: it exempts one band on the model from every rule that band trips.
The joker is spent once. A second band with no material behind it is a finding, whatever the first one was.
Spent on N4 it lifts the ceiling by one; every other band still answers to M and C. N2 and N3 do not count the joker as a material.
Only the PO assigns the tag. A special records which band it covers and why; one without a stated reason is a finding on the tag.
N3 leaves the joker's band out of its count; N2 keeps it. That band is the one the reason on the tag names.
env-flora-tree is dark green 1,1; env-flora-tree-palm follows M2.
env-flora-tree-palm fronds are light green 3,1.
env-flora-plant-grass is light green 3,1.
Stems and leaves are light green.
Wood is any of the three brown bands; wood-bark is bark 3,0.
Wood is any of the three brown bands; wood-bark is bark 3,0.
stone-masonry — walls, bricks, floors — is taupe 14,3, blue-grey 6,1 or light grey 15,3.
stone-rock is light grey 15,3, secondarily taupe 14,3.
stone-soil — sand and dirt — is taupe 14,3.
metal-iron-steel is light grey 15,3.
metal-iron-wrought is dark grey 13,3; metal-iron-cast is blue-grey 6,1.
metal-iron-wrought is dark grey 13,3; metal-iron-cast is blue-grey 6,1.
metal-gold is yellow 6,0; metal-silver is light blue-grey 3,2.
metal-gold is yellow 6,0; metal-silver is light blue-grey 3,2.
metal-copper is terracotta 5,0 and takes no other metal subtype.
metal-copper is terracotta 5,0 and takes no other metal subtype.
obj-pocketitem-key is metal-iron-wrought, dark grey 13,3, or metal-gold, yellow 6,0.
Hoops on obj-container-barrel, -chest, -bucket and -crate are metal-iron-wrought, dark grey 13,3.
Textile is off-white, taupe 14,3, dark green 1,1 or dark red 8,0.
Textile on obj-transport-ship, -boat and -accessory is off-white, dark green 1,1, dark red 8,0 or blue-grey 6,1 — never taupe 14,3.
Wrapped grips and bindings on tools and weapons are always taupe 14,3, light half 0.02-0.40.
Leather is bark.
Rope is taupe 14,3.
All cork is taupe 14,3.
Glass is transparent, dark green or dark red.
Ceramics are terracotta, off-white, taupe or dark red.
obj-container-bottle is glass or ceramic.
A glass obj-container-bottle is dark red 8,0, dark green 1,1 or clear glass.
A liquid is dark red 8,0, dark green 1,1 or blue 4,2.
Bone and env-remains-bones are off-white 5,2.
Paper is off-white.
obj-food-meat is dark red 8,0.
Flames, glow and lights are yellow 6,0, spread wide across the band.
Candle wax are off-white 5,2.
Wicks are dark grey 13,3.
Gemstones are dark red 8,0, dark green 1,1 or blue 4,2.
Covers of obj-pocketitem-book and obj-weapon-magic with paper are bark, dark red 8,0, dark green 1,1 or blue-grey 6,1.
str-part-roof is ceramic, dark red 8,0.
obj-container-barrel, -chest, -bucket and -crate are mainly wood, often with metal-iron accents.
Wood subtypes take their band: wood-planks 0,0, wood-worked 1,0, wood-beam 2,0. wood-log and wood-bark follow M6.
Wood subtypes take their band: wood-planks 0,0, wood-worked 1,0, wood-beam 2,0. wood-log and wood-bark follow M6.
Wood subtypes take their band: wood-planks 0,0, wood-worked 1,0, wood-beam 2,0. wood-log and wood-bark follow M6.
Skin is light brown 0,0, taupe 14,3 or bark 3,0.
Vegetation is a plant's non-green matter: dried stalks taupe 14,3, grain straw light brown (M51), blooms any colour. Fungi: M72.
obj-weapon, obj-equipment, obj-kitchenware-tableware and obj-tool are metal-iron-steel.
obj-tool-supplies is metal-iron-wrought; its parent kind stays steel.
obj-weapon-cannon and every str model with iron carry metal-iron-cast; another subtype may sit on top.
Metal cookware always exists as both steel and cast, paired as variants; a model keeps the iron it is.
Metal cookware always exists as both steel and cast, paired as variants; a model keeps the iron it is.
All other iron is metal-iron-wrought.
A model may carry more than one iron subtype; each counts under N2. Never merge two iron bands into one.
char iron is metal-iron-steel. An assembly answers per part; until it does, M66 stands.
Light grey 15,3: metal-iron-steel, stone, rock and fish (M83) only.
Blue-grey 6,1: cast iron (M12), worked stone (M8), book covers (M37), rigged-ship flags (M18b), scroll text (M86), fish (M83).
Light blue-grey 3,2: silver (M13).
Blue 4,2: sparingly, minor accents, scroll accents (M86) and fish (M83).
Yellow: metal-gold, emissive, fire and cheese (M83).
Dark red: ceramics, glass, str-part-roof, meat (M31), fungus caps (M72), textile (M70), gemstones (M36), minor accents.
Dark green: foliage, glass, textile only on character clothing or weapons (M18), and minor accents.
Light green: nature only — flora, grass and weed accents growing on objects and structures, and vegetables (M83).
Browns 0,0 1,0 2,0: wood, grain food (M51), chocolate (M84), fungus caps (M72); light brown 0,0 also skin (M43) and straw (M44).
Browns 0,0 1,0 2,0: wood, grain food (M51), chocolate (M84), fungus caps (M72); light brown 0,0 also skin (M43) and straw (M44).
Browns 0,0 1,0 2,0: wood, grain food (M51), chocolate (M84), fungus caps (M72); light brown 0,0 also skin (M43) and straw (M44).
Bark 3,0: wood-bark, leather, skin, wood-log and env-flora-deadwood.
Transparent: glass only.
Taupe 14,3: soil, rock (M9), masonry (M8), textile (M18), rope, cork, skin, dried vegetation (M44) and grips (M19).
Off-white 5,2: bone, paper, wax, ceramics (M25), textile (M18) and mushroom stems (M44).
Terracotta 5,0: copper (M14), ceramics (M25), carrot and pumpkin (M84) and blooms (M44).
Dark grey 13,3: metal-iron-wrought (M12), wicks (M35) and fish (M83).
A model has at least one material.
A model uses at least as many bands as it has materials. Every material tag counts, subtypes included.
A model uses at most twice as many bands as materials; food, fauna and vegetation may use three times, a decorated food five.
Ceiling: 6 bands for a human character or a decorated food, 5 for anything else. A skeleton takes the 5; an assembly answers per part.
A model of size l may take a sixth band where it carries at least five material tags.
